name: multicellularity
title: From Cells to Organisms

campaign_docs.name: From Cells to Organisms — Multicellularity Investigation Seed

lead: This investigation is a falsifiable simulation-and-evidence program for the emergence of multicellularity, synthesizing Morowitz's emergence framework with experimental evolution (snowflake yeast, predator-selected Chlamydomonas; volvocine algae and filamentous cyanobacteria as comparative systems) and biophysical modeling. It distinguishes well-supported observations from hypotheses, proposes interoperable mechanistic models compiled into process-bigraph composites, and specifies a first discovery cycle capable of REJECTING explanations. The first deliverable is a validated minimal cell-collective simulator and a claim-evidence graph.
question: Under what physical, metabolic, ecological, developmental, and evolutionary conditions can independent cells become a persistent, integrated, self-reproducing multicellular evolutionary individual? The existence of adherent cells is not sufficient to establish a major transition; a defensible investigation must identify a SEQUENCE of separately measurable properties — collective formation, physiological coordination, reproducible group reproduction, heritable group-level traits, and adaptation at the collective level — which may evolve in different orders and need not all appear in every lineage.
hypothesis: The transition is persuasive only when each property is demonstrated on plausible mechanistic terms and the combination is shown sufficient for persistence and further complexity. Discriminating objective: determine WHEN size-dependent ecological selection and elementary adhesion explain observed group formation, and WHEN metabolism, development, heritable life cycles, or conflict suppression are NECESSARY for persistence and further complexity. No single mechanism is assumed universally sufficient.
expert_docs: From Cells to Organisms — Multicellularity Investigation Seed

executive.what_is_this: Seed for a falsifiable program testing which conditions turn independent cells into an integrated, self-reproducing multicellular individual.
executive.verdict: First cycle: clonal adhesion produces persistent groups, but adhesion alone confers no fitness advantage; size-dependent ecological selection (predation/settling) is what makes groups fitter than unicells; oxygen/transport then bounds that advantage to an optimal intermediate group size.
executive.verdict_detail: Proposed seed — tool names and the import manifest are design targets, not a verified importer schema. No studies have run; every claim is provisional until mapped to source-specific evidence.
executive.objective: Reproduce group formation, fragmentation, and group-level fitness from first principles, and bound which constraint combinations are sufficient versus necessary for persistence and further complexity.
executive.central_gap: Separately measurable properties (formation, coordination, group reproduction, heritable group traits, collective adaptation) have not been demonstrated together on one mechanistically consistent system; it is unknown which combinations are sufficient, which necessary, and which merely possible.
executive.mandate: Test whether ecological selection plus simple clonal adhesion suffices to reproduce group formation and group-level fitness; compare competing mechanistic models; report non-identifiability and select a discriminating intervention rather than announcing discovery. Preserve the distinction among possibility, sufficiency, necessity, and historical inference.

decisions_needed.question: Which test system anchors the first cycle — snowflake yeast (settling) or predator-selected Chlamydomonas?
decisions_needed.context: S01/S02 benchmark against Ratcliff 2012 and Herron 2019; the anchor choice sets the ecological-selection treatment.

decisions_needed.question: Ingest the Bozdag 2023 source data/code (R8) and SRA PRJNA943273 (R9), or treat them as comparison-only?
decisions_needed.context: S03/S04 benchmark against Bozdag 2023 (oxygen, elongation, macroscopic size, mechanical robustness); direct ingestion enables held-out prediction.

decisions_resolved.question: Does ecological selection + simple clonal adhesion suffice for group formation and a group-level fitness advantage? (first-cycle A/B/C)
decisions_resolved.resolution: Discriminated on cell_collective: A (adhesion only) forms persistent groups (0.67) but adv~0; B (+predation/settling) gives adv>0 (+0.15); C (+O2-limited growth) bounds the advantage to small/intermediate size. Ecology is sufficient for the advantage; adhesion alone is not; transport sets a size optimum.

scientific_argument.main_claim: A major transition to multicellularity requires a sequence of separately measurable properties (formation, coordination, group reproduction, heritable group traits, collective adaptation) that can evolve in different orders; simulation under shared canonical states can bound which constraint combinations are sufficient versus necessary.
evidence_for: C1 Predation can favor groups (R4, experimental).
C3 Diffusion limits size (R3, R5 — physical premise + evidence).
C4 Mechanics permits macroscopic clusters (R5, direct yeast evidence).
C6 Life cycles sustain group selection (R2, R6 — theory + yeast data).
evidence_against: C5 Gradients-initiate-specialization is a mechanistic hypothesis without a demonstrated non-regulated null.
C7 Complexity-requires-integration rests on broad comparative inference and must avoid asserting a universal necessary pathway.
caveats: Reproducing multicellular phenotypes does not by itself establish the actual prehistoric sequence of evolutionary events. The program explicitly preserves the distinctions among possibility, sufficiency, necessity, and historical inference. S05 uses volvocine/cyanobacterial differentiation as qualitative comparison unless directly usable datasets are ingested; S06 does not imply historical reconstruction from present-day experiments.

findings.statement: Under size-dependent predation/settling, groups gain a FITNESS ADVANTAGE over unicells (adv=+0.15); with adhesion alone (no ecology) the advantage vanishes (adv=-0.00). Ecological selection — NOT adhesion per se — confers the group-level fitness advantage (supports H1 for the advantage).
findings.inferential_scope: Reduced mean-field cell-collective model (cell_collective): unicell/group split under adhesion + size-dependent predation/settling + oxygen-limited growth. First-fidelity; not an explicit spatial agent/mechanics simulation and not a historical estimate.

studies.name: s03-transport-limits
studies.title: Transport limits
studies.question: How do oxygen, nutrients, cell shape, packing and geometry limit collective size? (Q2)

findings.statement: Oxygen/transport BOUNDS the advantage to an optimal intermediate size: small groups (size=3.7) keep a positive advantage (adv=+0.12) while large groups (size=17.0) lose it (adv=-0.21). Size/viability tracks the transport regime (supports C3; the advantage is not monotonic in size).

studies.name: s04-morphomechanics
studies.title: Morphomechanics
studies.question: How do cell aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and bond strength set collective toughness and propagule size? (Q2)
methods: Cellular Potts (Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg) clonal growth with differential adhesion

findings.statement: In a Rust CPM clonal growth world, adhesion sets propagule toughness: seed-mean largest_cluster_fraction is 0.19 at adhesion 0, 0.57 at 0.3 and 1.0 (a single propagule) for adhesion >= 0.5; the zero-adhesion control fractures into 11-16 propagules.
findings.inferential_scope: Transient (~40-update), quasi-static readout of one CPM backend (viva-cpm); adhesion is the only swept knob (aspect ratio, topology, packing and cross-backend agreement untested). Fracture re-merges past ~80 updates.

studies.claim: Cell adhesion (homotypic contact energy) sets collective toughness: a clonal CPM cluster under growth-driven stress stays one cohesive propagule at strong adhesion and fractures into multiple propagules at weak adhesion. UNPROVEN until the adhesion x seed sweep is graded; aspect ratio, branch topology and cross-backend agreement (C4) are not tested here.

derived.insight: In a Rust CPM clonal growth world, adhesion sets propagule toughness: seed-mean largest_cluster_fraction is 0.19 at adhesion 0, 0.57 at 0.3 and 1.0 (a single propagule) for adhesion >= 0.5; the zero-adhesion control fractures into 11-16 propagules.

studies.name: s05-differentiation
studies.title: Cell-state differentiation
studies.question: Can environmental gradients create stable cell-state differentiation without a dedicated developmental program? (Q4, Q3)
methods: Cellular Potts patch with O2 diffusion/consumption; SBML stemness ODE + Boolean fate gate

findings.statement: In the oxygen arm an O2 gradient forms across the cluster and the interior differentiates: at update 40 there are 15 germ and 10 soma cells (~40% differentiated), with interior O2 ~0.57 vs rim ~0.86.
findings.inferential_scope: Single representative seed/environment readout (oxygen arm, update 40), transient quasi-static viva-cpm 2D window; the gradient and split are measured, not fit.

findings.statement: Mechanism: interior hypoxia makes the per-cell stemness ODE decay below the fixed threshold, cells switch to the low-O2-consumption soma fate, which frees O2 so that neighboring germ cells stay above the growth threshold and keep growing.
findings.inferential_scope: Mechanism is built into the model (engineered fate rule); the arms with fate off (none/clamped) lack the freed-O2 pathway and the random arm shows the placement matters. Not independently validated against data.

findings.statement: Interpretation: gradient-keyed specialization improves out-of-sample net viable growth in a moderate O2 regime, decisively over random fate and modestly (~5% on B) over no fate. The fate rule is designed (engineered); the yield benefit is emergent from the spatial O2 dynamics. It does not hold when O2 is plentiful and is unreliable when O2 is very scarce.
findings.inferential_scope: Two graded O2 regimes (A calibration, B held-out), 3 seeds, fixed a-priori threshold; off-grid regimes (0.03, 0.015) were probed informally only.

findings.statement: In a Rust CPM world with an O2 gradient, O2-keyed germ/soma differentiation beats all three nulls on the held-out environment B (o2_source 0.025): seed-mean net viable growth 285.0 (oxygen) vs 270.0 (no-fate), 270.0 (clamped-undifferentiated) and 159.7 (random-fate); out-of-sample gain +15.0. The benefit over the no-fate/clamped nulls is modest (~5%; ~20% on calibration env A: 195.7 vs 163.3); over random fate it is decisive (random soma wastes growth).
findings.inferential_scope: Transient ~40-update quasi-static readout of one CPM backend (viva-cpm), 2D, 3 seeds per arm. The stemness threshold is fixed a priori (not tuned to data), so this tests generalization across two O2 regimes, not a data-fit cross-validation. The benefit vanishes when O2 is plentiful (o2_source 0.03, no hypoxia, oxygen == none) and degrades/noisy when O2 is very scarce (0.015, over-differentiation, ~20/25 soma); those regimes were probed informally, not in the graded runs. Metric choice (net viable growth) is owner-sanctioned ruling S05-B.

studies.claim: In a 2D CPM world with an O2 gradient, O2-keyed germ/soma specialization (fixed a-priori stemness threshold) improves net viable growth out-of-sample on held-out env B (o2_source 0.025): decisively over a random-fate null and modestly (~5%) over a no-fate / clamped-undifferentiated null, in a moderate O2 regime. The benefit vanishes when O2 is plentiful and degrades when O2 is very scarce; transient 40-update window, one CPM backend.

derived.insight: In the oxygen arm an O2 gradient forms across the cluster and the interior differentiates: at update 40 there are 15 germ and 10 soma cells (~40% differentiated), with interior O2 ~0.57 vs rim ~0.86.

studies.name: s06-individuality
studies.title: Evolutionary individuality
studies.question: Does generational group selection on a heritable adhesion trait produce a response that requires clonal group structure (evolutionary individuality)? (Q5)
methods: Generational group selection on cell adhesion (CPM groups, Price partition)
discovery_implications: If supported, clonal group structure plus selection suffices for a heritable group-level response; whether non-clonal groups can sustain it depends on conflict mechanics not modelled here.

findings.statement: Seed-mean mean-adhesion response over 6 generations (held-out seeds 4-6 | training seeds 1-3): clonal+selection +0.224 | +0.324; clonal drift null +0.101 | -0.008; mixed+selection +0.138 | +0.096; mixed drift +0.101 | -0.008. Group toughness: clonal-sel ~0.93, clonal-drift ~0.82. All 24 runs completed; numbers from analysis/grade_individuality.py.
findings.inferential_scope: 6 generations, 6 potts seeds per arm, one CPM backend (viva-cpm), 2D.

findings.statement: Mechanism: group fitness = largest-cluster toughness (reuses S04 fracture); the Price partition splits the group-adhesion change into among-group (Cov(w,z)) and within-group (E[w*dz]) terms. among_group is positive for selection arms and ~0 for drift; within_group is ~0 in EVERY arm because adhesion carries no intrinsic within-group growth advantage under uniform growth. Heritability (parent-offspring regression of group adhesion) is 1.0 clonal / 0.5 mixed, fixed by the clonal/mixed encoding (structural, not emergent).
findings.inferential_scope: Engineered generational loop; Price terms computed, not validated against data.

findings.statement: Clonal group-level selection evolves a heritable adhesion increase (individuality emerges) that the drift null does not; clonality is required (mixed response attenuated, heritability halved). QUALIFIED — the clean selection-over-drift margin is on training seeds (+0.33); on held-out seeds the drift null drifts up ~+0.10 (boundary reflection of the [0,0.6] init), leaving a modest +0.12 margin. The mixed (non-clonal) control collapses heritability by trait DILUTION, not active within-group conflict (R-S06-DILUTION): with adhesion as the only trait, cheaters have no within-group fitness advantage.
findings.inferential_scope: Seeds 4-6 held out; 6-generation horizon; 2D; one CPM backend; a-priori-fixed parameters.

studies.claim: Clonal group-level selection on a heritable adhesion set-point produces a multi-generation evolutionary response: seed-mean mean-adhesion rises +0.22 on held-out seeds 4-6 (+0.32 on training seeds 1-3) over 6 generations, exceeding the selection-off drift null and reaching the highest group cohesion (toughness ~0.93). Clonality is required for full trait transmission (heritability 1.0 clonal vs 0.5 mixed) and the mixed-founder response is attenuated (+0.14 held-out). QUALIFIED: the clean selection-vs-drift margin is on training seeds (+0.33 over a ~0 null); on held-out seeds the drift null itself drifts up ~+0.10 (boundary reflection of the lower-bounded [0,0.6] init), narrowing the held-out margin to +0.12. Heritability is structural (fixed by the clonal/mixed encoding), not emergent; the emergent result is the response. within_group is ~0 in every arm, so non-clonal founding collapses heritability by trait dilution, not active within-group conflict.

derived.insight: Seed-mean mean-adhesion response over 6 generations (held-out seeds 4-6 | training seeds 1-3): clonal+selection +0.224 | +0.324; clonal drift null +0.101 | -0.008; mixed+selection +0.138 | +0.096; mixed drift +0.101 | -0.008. Group toughness: clonal-sel ~0.93, clonal-drift ~0.82. All 24 runs completed; numbers from analysis/grade_individuality.py.
